files.reason: This lane's copy-record fragment (interface 1). Lane blindness-sidechains (the Lane-orchestrator's ruling of Sat 24 Oct 2026, under Javier's standing delegation, after pre-freeze round 1's blindness record read 45 UNEXPLAINED hits, each one inside a queued_command attachment carrying a sub-agent's hand-back, and blindness.py had never read the sub-agents' own sessions). Edits without transfer, in three files lane review-kit-port's fragment claims. review_kit/blindness.py reads every sidechain session the reviewer's session spawned (records marked isSidechain, and <session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl, matched to the Agent tool's results; a launched agent with no session file and a session file no launch names are each stated) and applies the same markers and the same absolute-path scan to each. A hand-back is read on its own, whichever record carries it (a user message, a queued command read once from its rendered form, a task notification, a foreground Agent result): a hit there is explained only when the word or path it sits in occurs in a file that was in the folder at launch and that no session wrote, and in that sub-agent's own tool traffic; an absolute path outside the folder never traces. The operator rows (lane-orchestrator, Lane Board, OrgOS, Waiting on Javier, glitch-mem, SOUL.md, north star, MEMORY.md, this repository by path, and a new row for the operator's Brain by path) are never explained, in a hand-back or in any loaded context. Writes outside the folder are listed in their own section and void nothing by themselves, and a last section states what the sub-agents' records show of the reviewer's isolation. The reviewer's launch flags are unchanged. tests/test_review_kit.py gains K15.sidechains, written red first, over one fixture reviewer session with five sub-agent session files, with 22 witnesses each red by K15.sidechains alone. review_kit/README.md's step 5 names the sidechain sessions and the sections that bind. Folds of the review of 5a6dc21 (VERDICT CHANGES, lanes/REVIEW-blindness-sidechains-5a6dc21.md; the Lane-orchestrator's rulings of Sat 24 Oct 2026, under Javier's standing delegation): a path tail must still hold the marker it explains; the folder is the folder as it stood at launch, from launch.py's per-file manifest when there is one, otherwise the files no newer than the launch stamp and written by no session through any tool, the shell included, and the record names the rule that ran; a report read through TaskOutput or its tasks/<id>.output file is a hand-back, read once; an Agent result that names no agent is listed in section 2 and stays UNEXPLAINED; a sub-agent read only what its tool results hold, never its own inputs; a relayed nested hand-back traces through the nested agent's own session, and a missing one explains nothing; a record kept twice and a reflowed rendered form are read once; the docstring states the shared study-word limit; section 4 counts the reports and lists task notifications apart. review_kit/launch.py (lane review-kit-port's entry) gains write_manifest, called once at launch, which writes folder-manifest.txt beside folder-at-launch.txt: one sha256 and path line per regular file, never a .git folder or a link. tests/test_review_kit.py gains class SidechainFolds, twelve tests written red first at 5a6dc21 (9 failures, 3 errors), with 21 more witnesses each red by K15.sidechains alone. language-allowlist.json gains four entries for the committed review's ratio-slash lines (each bound to its exact text). The lead's ruling on the brief (Sat 24 Oct 2026): a hand-back hit the sub-agent did not read but its brief holds is traced via brief when its extent is explained for the brief's author, in a tool result that session received or in the launch corpus, and section 4 prints it in its own column. The shell write rule reads a command step by step: a cp, mv or rsync writes only its destination, a step that writes only by a redirect writes only the redirect's target, and a step that names no absolute path writes where an earlier cd of the same command left it. Two more K15 tests (both red at 97a1bd29) and eight more witnesses. Folds of the closure review of fff7e0d3 (the Lane-orchestrator's rulings the same day): a shell step's cwd starts at the record's own cwd and follows every cd, and its relative targets are read against it inside the folder too, so a relative redirect, tee, here-document or date-keeping copy (cp -p, rsync -a, tar -x, with its target folder and all it holds) leaves the corpus; section 6 counts a program's --out, --output or -o argument (never a reader's), a tar -x or unzip destination (-C, -d or the cwd), and reads &> and >> as redirects, while a here-document's body is data, not steps; on the brief route a hit counts as explained only when its extent is in the launch corpus. review_kit/rounds.py (lane w7d-rehearsals' entry) writes folder-manifest.txt beside the folder in --add before it hashes the row, and the row's input_sha256 is that manifest's digest (manifest_digest; folder_sha256's value is unchanged), so the committed row binds the manifest with no new field; review_kit/launch.py no longer writes a manifest and refuses to launch a folder that no longer matches it; blindness.py names the round row whose input_sha256 the manifest reproduces, or says it binds nothing. Five more K15 tests or cases written red first at fff7e0d3 (5 failures, 1 error), and the witness registry re-anchored and grown to 105.

The review kit's round register (review_kit/rounds.py's own file, one row per round of blind review, append-only), first written by 96c1d959 (prefreeze round 1: register the row before its reviewer opens) with no fragment claiming it, so copy_manifest --check read it unclaimed on every later lane. Claimed here on the Lane-orchestrator's ruling 4 of Sat 24 Oct 2026 (under Javier's standing delegation); its bytes are not changed by this claim, and each later row is appended by rounds.py --add.
